result:
The command needs admin privileges. Here's what you need to do:

1. **Open PowerShell as Administrator** (right-click PowerShell → "Run as Administrator")
2. **Run this command:**

```powershell
$scriptPath = "/home/author/Documents/GitHub/repo\.campaign\sandbox\w1\persist.autostart-v1-178662393923368\scripts\sync.sh"
$taskName = "SyncScript-Every15Min"
$bashPath = "C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe"

if (-not (Test-Path $bashPath)) {
    $bashPath = "bash"
}

$action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $bashPath -Argument "`"$scriptPath`""
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -RepetitionInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 15) -At (Get-Date) -Once
$startupTrigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtStartup
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries -StartWhenAvailable

Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName $taskName -Action $action -Trigger @($trigger, $startupTrigger) -Settings $settings -Description "Run sync script every 15 minutes" -Force

Write-Host "Task created: $taskName runs every 15 minutes and at startup"
```

This will create a scheduled task that:
- Runs `scripts/sync.sh` every 15 minutes
- Automatically runs at system startup
- Persists across reboots
- Continues running even on battery

To verify it was created, run: `Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "SyncScript-Every15Min"` or check Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc).
